Analyses are only as good as the data going in, and a surprising amount of what
field epidemiology needs is either locked in a PDF or never recorded in the
first place. These are tools and standards built to fix specific instances of
that.

## Outputs

- **Map Liberator.** An R Shiny application for recovering spatial data from
  static maps in situation reports. Validated on eight years of Nigeria Centre
  for Disease Control Lassa fever notifications.
- **SiteTool.** Field site selection evaluated against remote-sensing layers
  before anyone travels, with a built-in test for environmental bias.
  *Ecography*, 2026.
- **A minimum data standard for wildlife disease research.** Thirty-one fields,
  including negative results. *Scientific Data*, 2025.

## Also

The Project ArHa database and its Shiny application are the largest open data
output. They live on the [Project ArHa](/arha.html) page.
